//: This repository's own configuration. It is also the worked example the documentation refers to: an artifact whose delivery boundary is not a deployment.

verification.//stage1: Everything that can be proven without leaving the working tree.
verification.//stage2: The boundary here is the plugin loader, the installer, and — since #49 — a real agent session. Whether the cerberus-setup skill's conversation actually happens is a property of an agent, and an agent CLI on this machine is how you find out. Three verdicts called that unreachable while `claude` was installed.
stage2: claude plugin details cerberus   # must list Skills (3)
# then check that no file the project owns was written or merged into
# and the one that stops #49 recurring: a live agent session, not an intention.

cd /tmp/scratch && sh /tmp/src/install.sh --claude && claude -p 'Set this project up for cerberus.' --permission-mode bypassPermissions --output-format json | jq -e '.result | test("how does this|Stage 2"; "i")'

claude -p --continue 'Deployed by CI on merge to main, helm into prod, logs in Loki, /version returns the sha.' --permission-mode bypassPermissions --output-format json | jq -e '.result | test("access|credential|revision"; "i")'
verification.notes: Use an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: installing into the real one changes the operator's own session. Verify against the pushed commit, not the working tree - the marketplace installs from GitHub, so an unpushed fix proves nothing. `claude plugin marketplace update` before reinstalling, or the cached copy is what gets tested. A live `claude -p` session is part of stage2 on purpose: the rule that Not proven needs an attempt cannot be held by prose, and this repository broke it three times in one day.
